summary: This note is a short biography of John C. Petersen (1842–1887), an American butcher and farmer from Appleton, Wisconsin. He served in the Wisconsin State Assembly representing Outagamie County. He was first elected in 1878 as a Greenbacker and re-elected the following year as a "Greenback Democrat" despite facing a Democratic opponent.
one_line: John C. Petersen was a Wisconsin butcher, farmer, and Greenback-affiliated member of the State Assembly from Outagamie County.
key_facts: John C. Petersen was born on November 2, 1842.
John C. Petersen died on July 10, 1887.
John C. Petersen was an American butcher and farmer from Appleton, Wisconsin.
John C. Petersen served as a member of the Wisconsin State Assembly from Outagamie County.
John C. Petersen was elected to the Wisconsin State Assembly in 1878 as a Greenbacker.
John C. Petersen was re-elected to the Wisconsin State Assembly the next year as a "Greenback Democrat".
John C. Petersen was re-elected as a Greenback Democrat even though he was opposed by a Democrat.
